newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO FANS GRAFITTI PROTEST AGAINST TOSHACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO FANS GRAFITTI PROTEST AGAINST TOSHACK.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna's Riazor stadium has been daubed with grafitti criticising coach John Toshack after the Welshman announced his intention to leave the club at the end of the season.
Toshack is believed to have received offers from several other clubs, while his announcement has sparked rumours linking former Barcelona coach Johan Cruyff with Deportivo.
Speculation is also rife that Brazilian striker Bebeto is considering a return to his old team.
"Toshack go home," read some of the grafitti which was written in English and echoed a similar protest made against Barcelona's Bobby Robson last month.
Toshack tried to limit the damage done to his already poor relationship with Deportivo fans at a press conference on Tuesday.

"The supporters are always right, they pay, and so we get paid....saying they've been injust with me is not an insult," said Toshack, who had already tried to pour oil on troubled waters at a dinner with Deportivo president Augusto Lendoiro.
The former Real Sociedad and Real Madrid coach stressed his initial remarks had been misinterpreted.
"On June 30 (when his contract ends) I could be on the beach, or at a bullfight, or playing golf...nobody's spoken to me yet," said Toshack.
An article in the Spanish sports daily 'Marca' on Tuesday listed Manchester City, Blackburn and Sporting Lisbon among clubs interested in securing the services of the former Liverpool striker.
Toshack's difficulties with the Deportivo crowd stem in part from repeated clashes with Bebeto who had been a key figure in the line-up of predecessor Arsenio Iglesias.
Bebeto left Deportivo in the close season but failed to settle at Brazilian club Flamengo and has struggled since joining Sevilla in November.
Ironically, Bebeto twisted his ankle in training on Tuesday and will be absent from Wednesday's Spanish Cup tie against Deportivo.
By playing his fifth competitive match this season for Sevilla, Bebeto would have been automatically excluded from the Spanish transfer market.
But the injury means Deportivo will have a few more days to think about signing the Brazilian.
Bebeto said on Tuesday he was "a little worried" by Sevilla's financial problems. Sevilla have had difficulties in paying Flamengo his transfer fee.
